api-audit.title: API & integration audit
api-audit.description: We review your APIs, authentication, timeouts, retries, webhooks, idempotency, logs, and monitoring. You leave with a Technical Integration Report: problems, risks, quick wins, target architecture, roadmap.
api-audit.audience: Teams whose public or partner APIs are getting harder to change without breaking clients.
api-audit.guarantee: If the report teaches you nothing, we do not invoice.
features: Map of API contracts and breaking points
OAuth2 / JWT, errors, timeouts, and retries

payment-audit.title: Payment Architecture Audit
payment-audit.description: From payment request to settlement: API, provider, webhook, transaction, ledger, reconciliation. You get an Architecture Assessment, a Risk Map, and a Technical Roadmap — plus a Payment Reliability Score.
payment-audit.audience: FinTech, PSPs, mobile money, wallets, aggregators, and platforms that actually collect money.
payment-audit.guarantee: If the report teaches you nothing, we do not invoice.
features: Reliability score by domain, out of 100
Duplicate payments, replayed webhooks, inconsistent states

architecture-review.title: Architecture review

architecture-review.audience: Teams for whom every change is getting risky, slow, or politically hard to start.

production-audit.title: Production reliability audit
production-audit.description: Timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, observability, high availability, runbooks. You leave with a Production Reliability Report — what will break, how you will know, and how long recovery takes.
production-audit.audience: Production platforms that still learn about incidents from a customer ticket.
features: Timeout, retry, circuit breaker, rate-limiting review

security-audit.title: API security audit
security-audit.description: OAuth2, JWT, RBAC, API gateway, secrets, webhook authentication, OWASP API Security. Findings ranked Critical / High / Medium / Low, with a remediation plan.
security-audit.audience: Platforms exposing APIs to partners, mobile apps, or payment providers.

performance-audit.title: Performance engineering

performance-audit.audience: Platforms whose latency, throughput, or infrastructure cost is starting to block growth.

reconciliation-diagnostic.title: Reconciliation diagnostic

golive-review.title: Go-live readiness review

transparency.title: Two engagements at a time. Zero handoffs.
transparency.intro: In payment systems, the expensive failures come from lost context — the person who understood the constraint is rarely the person who ships the code. We cap ourselves at two engagements so that gap never opens: the engineer who maps your architecture is the one who implements it.
transparency.gains: Named senior engineers, from the first call to go-live. The person who maps your architecture writes the code, owns the deployment and answers after launch. No sales layer, no account manager, no junior assigned by default.
transparency.costsTitle: Where we are not the right fit
transparency.costs: Two engagements in parallel, no more. If you need a ten-person team staffed next week, a 24/7 on-call rotation, or a vendor to answer a 200-page RFP, we are not it — and you will hear that on the first call, not three weeks in.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Capacity, partnerships, pricing, references, and timing.

young.question: Why trust a recent firm with a critical system?
young.answer: Because the liability is contractual and verifiable: milestone payments, code on your repository from day one, a 60-day fix warranty, and an initial audit refunded if it teaches you nothing. A short engagement lets you judge the work before widening the scope.

pricing.question: Why are your prices not listed?
pricing.answer: Because the amount depends on criticality, the state of what you already have, and the volume you process. The same audit is not priced the same for an early-stage platform and for a high-volume aggregator. After a 45-minute scoping call, you receive a priced proposal within 48 hours — a firm figure, not a vague range.

capacity.question: There are only two of you. What if one of you is unavailable?
capacity.answer: All of our code lives on your repository, documented so a third party can take over. We create no dependency on our presence — that is a design rule, not a sales promise. We also cap ourselves at two concurrent projects so we are never overcommitted.

partners.question: We are an agency / SI. Do you subcontract?
partners.answer: Yes — on collection only. You keep the prime contract and the relationship. We come in as the named specialist: audit, rails, webhooks, reconciliation. Report under your name or ours. We do not take the rest of the project, and we do not contact your client to capture the account.

references.question: Can you give us client references?
references.answer: No client references to display yet. What we can show: the architecture of Xaalis, a financial product designed and built in-house, upcoming papers, and public laboratories in progress. A short technical review of your platform is another way to judge the work itself.

region.question: Do you work with companies outside Senegal?
region.answer: Yes. Dakar first, then WAEMU, and remotely beyond. Payment and FinTech platforms are naturally regional.

start.question: How soon can you start?
start.answer: Our next availability window is September 2026. An audit can typically start within two weeks.

payment-integration.metaDescription: A unified integration layer: idempotency, webhooks, retries and state management across providers.
payment-integration.headline: Payment integration platform
payment-integration.subheadline: One layer to orchestrate providers with inconsistent APIs and transaction states.
payment-integration.context: The client collected through several providers whose API contracts, webhooks and transaction statuses were not aligned. Each new rail added debt and incidents that were hard to explain to the business.
payment-integration.approach: We put a single integration layer in place: idempotency, retries, webhook normalisation and a shared state model. Providers become adapters, not the core of the system.
outcomes: A single integration contract for product teams
Retries and idempotency across every rail
A new provider can be added without rewriting the business

greenfield-platform.metaDescription: Orchestration, ledger and integration designed from scratch for a marketplace.
greenfield-platform.headline: Greenfield payment platform
greenfield-platform.subheadline: Orchestration, ledger and integration designed from scratch — observability and idempotency from day one.
greenfield-platform.context: A marketplace needed to collect across several rails with no existing payment infrastructure. The job was not to assemble SDKs: it needed a system that could hold settlement, reconciliation and scale.
greenfield-platform.approach: We designed orchestration, ledger and integration as one product. Idempotency, webhooks and observability were not bolted on later: they were in the first increment shipped.
outcomes: A production-ready payment stack, delivered incrementally
Ledger and orchestration aligned from the start
A scalable base for adding rails without a big bang

backend-modernization.metaDescription: A progressive stack upgrade without a big bang: APIs, events and observability, while keeping the existing system in service.
backend-modernization.headline: Production backend modernization
backend-modernization.subheadline: A progressive stack upgrade, without cutting service or rewriting what still holds.
backend-modernization.context: The production backend still ran the business but blocked change: fragile APIs, little observability, and a justified fear of a big bang. It had to be modernised without interrupting collection.
backend-modernization.approach: We isolated the seams, introduced APIs and events at the edges, then shifted traffic progressively. Each step had a rollback criterion and measurable observability.
outcomes: Service kept running throughout the migration
APIs and events in place on the critical path
Enough observability to operate without guesswork
A technical roadmap the internal team can continue

xaalis.metaDescription: A personal finance application for the WAEMU market: double-entry ledger in XOF, ingestion without open banking.
xaalis.headline: Xaalis
xaalis.subheadline: A personal finance application for the WAEMU market. Designed and built entirely in-house.
xaalis.context: There is no useful open banking in the WAEMU zone. To build a personal finance product that holds, transactions have to be ingested another way: Android notifications, operator SMS, bank statements — then held in an XOF ledger.
xaalis.approach: We designed an append-only double-entry ledger, envelope budgeting, and multiple income streams. Ingestion depends on no third-party bank API. It is an internal product, demonstrable, that exercises exactly the skill we sell: financial systems, idempotency, reconciliation, XOF.
outcomes: Envelope budgeting and multiple income streams
Ingestion without open banking: Android notifications, operator SMS, statement import
Designed and built entirely in-house — demonstrable on video
